text: The Extended Fund Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan by the IMF Executive Board in September 2024 was worth approximately how much?
explanation: The IMF Board approved a 37-month Extended Arrangement of SDR 5,320 million, about US$7 billion, on 25 September 2024.

text: What is the duration of the Extended Fund Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan in September 2024?
explanation: The arrangement was approved as a 37-month Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility.

text: Which IMF programme did Pakistan complete immediately before entering the 2024 Extended Fund Facility?
options: A nine-month Stand-By Arrangement of about US$3 billion
A Rapid Financing Instrument of about US$1.4 billion
A Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust loan
A Flexible Credit Line of about US$6 billion
explanation: Pakistan completed a nine-month Stand-By Arrangement of about US$3 billion, approved in July 2023, before the 2024 Extended Fund Facility.

text: In May 2025 the IMF Executive Board approved for Pakistan, alongside the first EFF review, an arrangement under which facility?
explanation: On 9 May 2025 the Board completed the first EFF review and approved a new arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, which finances climate-related reforms.

text: The Resilience and Sustainability Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan in May 2025 was worth approximately how much?
explanation: The RSF arrangement was approved at about US$1.4 billion to support climate-resilience reforms.

text: The IMF disbursement released to Pakistan on completion of the first review of the Extended Fund Facility in May 2025 was approximately how much?
explanation: Completion of the first EFF review on 9 May 2025 allowed an immediate disbursement of about US$1 billion (SDR 760 million).

text: In which month did the IMF Executive Board complete the second review of Pakistan's Extended Fund Facility, unlocking a tranche of about US$1.2 billion?
explanation: The Board completed the second EFF review and the first RSF review on 8 December 2025, releasing about US$1.2 billion.

text: The IMF Executive Board completed the third review of Pakistan's Extended Fund Facility in May 2026, approving a total immediate disbursement of about how much?
explanation: The 8 May 2026 decision released about US$1.1 billion under the EFF and about US$220 million under the RSF, roughly US$1.32 billion in total.

text: After the third EFF review in May 2026, total IMF disbursements to Pakistan under the EFF and RSF arrangements stood at approximately how much?
explanation: Cumulative disbursements under the two arrangements reached about US$4.8 billion (SDR 3,348 million) after the May 2026 decision.

text: What was the total outlay of Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: The FY2025-26 federal budget carried a total outlay of about Rs17.573 trillion, some 7 percent lower than the previous year's budget.

text: What tax collection target was set for the Federal Board of Revenue in the federal budget for 2025-26?
explanation: The FY2025-26 budget set an FBR revenue target of Rs14,131 billion, about 9 percent above the previous year's target.

text: How much was allocated to defence in Pakistan's federal budget for 2025-26?
explanation: Defence was allocated Rs2,550 billion in the FY2025-26 budget, an increase of about 20 percent over the previous year.

text: What real GDP growth target did the government set in the federal budget for 2025-26?
explanation: The FY2025-26 budget targeted real GDP growth of 4.2 percent; actual growth came in lower.

text: What inflation target was set for fiscal year 2025-26 in Pakistan's federal budget?
explanation: The FY2025-26 budget assumed average inflation of 7.5 percent for the year.

text: The federal budget for 2025-26 set the fiscal deficit target at what share of GDP?
explanation: The FY2025-26 budget targeted a fiscal deficit of 3.9 percent of GDP, down from a 5.9 percent target the previous year.

text: Which new levy on petroleum products was introduced in Pakistan's federal budget for 2025-26?
explanation: The FY2025-26 budget imposed a carbon levy of Rs2.50 per litre on petrol, diesel and furnace oil.

text: What pay increase was announced for federal government employees in grades 1 to 20 in the 2025-26 federal budget?
explanation: The FY2025-26 budget granted a 10 percent pay rise to federal employees in grades 1-20 and a 7 percent increase in pensions.

text: What was the total outlay of Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2026-27?
explanation: The FY2026-27 federal budget carried a total outlay of about Rs18.771 trillion, roughly 7 percent higher than the previous year.

text: Who presented Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2026-27 in the National Assembly?
explanation: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb presented the FY2026-27 budget in June 2026.

text: In which month was Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27 presented?
explanation: The FY2026-27 budget was presented in June 2026, in line with the usual budget calendar.

text: What FBR tax collection target was set in Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
explanation: The FY2026-27 budget set an FBR target of about Rs15.26 trillion, some 8 percent above the previous year's target.

text: How much was allocated to defence in Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
explanation: Defence spending was set at about Rs3 trillion in the FY2026-27 budget, an increase of roughly 15.6 percent.

text: The federal budget for 2026-27 set the fiscal deficit target at what share of GDP?
explanation: The FY2026-27 budget targeted a fiscal deficit of 3.6 percent of GDP alongside a primary surplus of 2 percent of GDP.

text: To what level was the monthly minimum wage raised in Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
explanation: The FY2026-27 budget raised the minimum wage from Rs37,000 to Rs40,700 per month.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, what was the country's real GDP growth in fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: The Economic Survey 2025-26 recorded provisional GDP growth of 3.7 percent, the fastest in four years but short of the 4.2 percent target.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, per capita income in FY2025-26 rose to approximately what level?
explanation: Per capita income was reported at about US$1,901 in FY2025-26, up from about US$1,751 the previous year.

text: What poverty rate did the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26 report for the country?
explanation: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that poverty had risen to 28.9 percent.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, total public debt at the end of March 2026 stood at approximately how much?
explanation: Total public debt was reported at about Rs83,285 billion, roughly Rs83 trillion, at end-March 2026.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, what was Pakistan's real GDP growth in fiscal year 2024-25?
explanation: The Economic Survey 2024-25 put provisional GDP growth for FY2024-25 at 2.68 percent.

text: What were Pakistan's total merchandise exports in fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics data put FY2025-26 exports at about US$30.126 billion, down nearly 6 percent year-on-year.

text: What were Pakistan's total merchandise imports in fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: Imports rose about 7.9 percent to roughly US$69.6 billion in FY2025-26.

text: Pakistan's merchandise trade deficit in fiscal year 2025-26 was approximately how large?
explanation: The trade deficit widened by about 21.6 percent to roughly US$39.5 billion in FY2025-26.

text: Workers' remittances to Pakistan in fiscal year 2025-26 reached what record level?
explanation: The State Bank reported record remittances of about US$41.6 billion in FY2025-26, a rise of roughly 8.6 percent.

text: Which country was the largest single source of workers' remittances to Pakistan in fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: Saudi Arabia sent about US$9.78 billion in FY2025-26, ahead of the UAE at about US$8.81 billion.

text: Pakistan's exports of information technology and IT-enabled services crossed which milestone for the first time in fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: IT and IT-enabled services exports set a record above US$4 billion in FY2025-26, up from about US$3.8 billion the previous year.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, the average rupee-dollar exchange rate in FY2025-26 was approximately what?
explanation: The Survey reported an average exchange rate of about Rs281.1 per US dollar during FY2025-26.

text: What was the State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate after the Monetary Policy Committee decision of April 2026?
explanation: The MPC raised the policy rate by 100 basis points to 11.5 percent in April 2026 and held it there in subsequent meetings.

text: The State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate increase in April 2026 was the first rise in the rate since which year?
explanation: The 100 basis point increase in April 2026 was Pakistan's first policy rate hike since June 2023.

text: What was the peak level of the State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate before the monetary easing cycle that began in June 2024?
explanation: The policy rate peaked at 22 percent, held from June 2023 until the first cut in June 2024.

text: In August 2025 Moody's upgraded Pakistan's sovereign credit rating to which level?
explanation: Moody's raised Pakistan's rating from Caa2 to Caa1 in August 2025, citing an improving external position.

text: In April 2025 Fitch Ratings upgraded Pakistan's long-term sovereign credit rating to which level?
explanation: Fitch upgraded Pakistan from CCC+ to B- with a stable outlook in April 2025, and later affirmed that rating.

text: In July 2026 S&P Global Ratings upgraded Pakistan's long-term sovereign credit rating from B- to which level?
explanation: S&P raised Pakistan's long-term sovereign rating to B with a stable outlook in July 2026, citing stronger institutional capacity for reform.

text: In May 2026 Pakistan issued its first ever Panda bond. In which market and currency was it issued?
options: Hong Kong's offshore market, in US dollars
explanation: A Panda bond is a renminbi-denominated bond sold by a foreign issuer in China's onshore capital market; Pakistan debuted there in May 2026.

text: How much did Pakistan raise through its inaugural Panda bond issued in May 2026?
explanation: Pakistan raised RMB 1.75 billion, about US$250 million, in its debut Panda bond, which was more than five times oversubscribed.

text: Which consortium won the bid to acquire a majority stake in Pakistan International Airlines in December 2025?
options: A consortium led by Arif Habib
A consortium led by Fauji Foundation
A consortium led by Serene Air
explanation: An Arif Habib-led consortium won the PIA privatisation bid in December 2025 with an offer of Rs135 billion.

text: What was the winning bid amount for the majority stake in Pakistan International Airlines offered in December 2025?
explanation: The winning consortium bid Rs135 billion for a 75 percent stake, against a government reference price of Rs100 billion.

text: Which mobile operator did Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited acquire under a transaction cleared by the Competition Commission of Pakistan in 2025?
explanation: The Competition Commission of Pakistan approved PTCL's acquisition of Telenor Pakistan in 2025, consolidating the mobile market.

text: The Rs1.225 trillion financing deal that the government signed with commercial banks in 2025 was intended to retire debt in which sector?
explanation: The deal with a consortium of commercial banks was designed to clear a large part of the power sector's circular debt.

text: In April 2025 the Prime Minister announced a reduction in electricity tariffs of approximately how much per unit?
explanation: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a cut of Rs7.41 per unit in electricity prices in early April 2025.

text: Mainline-1, the railway upgrade project under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, runs between which two cities?
explanation: ML-1 is the roughly 1,700-kilometre Karachi-Peshawar main railway line, the largest infrastructure project under CPEC.

text: In September 2025 Pakistan and China agreed to finance the ML-1 railway project through a consortium including which two multilateral lenders?
explanation: The agreed financing consortium for the roughly US$7 billion ML-1 project included the Asian Development Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank alongside China and Pakistan.

text: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor was formally launched during a visit by the Chinese President in which year?
explanation: CPEC agreements were signed during President Xi Jinping's visit to Pakistan in April 2015.

text: The Reko Diq copper and gold project is located in which district of Balochistan?
explanation: Reko Diq lies in Chagai district in western Balochistan, near the borders with Iran and Afghanistan.

text: Which company holds a 50 percent stake and operates the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Pakistan?
explanation: Under the 2022 reconstituted arrangement, Barrick holds 50 percent of Reko Diq and operates it, with the remainder split between federal entities and Balochistan.

text: The 34 memoranda of understanding signed between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in October 2024 were valued at approximately how much?
explanation: The October 2024 agreements were reported at a combined value of about US$2.8 billion.

text: In February 2025 Pakistan signed an agreement with Saudi Arabia to defer payment for oil imports worth approximately how much?
explanation: Pakistan signed an agreement in February 2025 for a US$1.2 billion Saudi oil facility on deferred payment terms.

text: In October 2025 Pakistan and Saudi Arabia launched which economic arrangement?
explanation: The two countries launched a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Framework in October 2025 covering trade, investment, energy, mining and IT.

text: At the ECO summit in July 2025 Pakistan signed an investment agreement with which country worth about US$2 billion?
explanation: Pakistan and Azerbaijan signed a US$2 billion investment agreement on the sidelines of the ECO summit in July 2025.

text: Under the trade arrangement announced with the United States in July 2025, Pakistani exports to the US were made subject to a tariff of what rate?
explanation: The July 2025 arrangement set a 19 percent tariff on Pakistani goods entering the United States, lower than the rate initially threatened.

text: Which sector featured prominently in the July 2025 Pakistan-United States trade understanding besides tariff reduction?
explanation: The understanding included cooperation on developing Pakistan's oil and gas reserves alongside the tariff arrangement.

text: In December 2024 the Prime Minister launched which five-year national economic transformation plan?
explanation: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched 'Uraan Pakistan', the National Economic Transformation Plan 2024-29, on 31 December 2024.

text: The Uraan Pakistan plan launched in December 2024 is built around a framework known by what name?
explanation: Uraan Pakistan is organised around the 5Es: Exports, E-Pakistan, Environment and climate, Energy and infrastructure, and Equity and empowerment.

text: The Uraan Pakistan plan sets a target of raising annual exports to approximately what level by 2029?
explanation: Uraan Pakistan aims to roughly double exports to about US$60 billion a year by 2029.

text: Under the National Tariff Policy 2025-30, the maximum customs duty slab is to be brought down to what rate?
explanation: The policy reduces the tariff structure to four slabs with a maximum rate of 15 percent over five years.

text: Which two import levies is Pakistan's National Tariff Policy 2025-30 designed to phase out entirely?
options: Regulatory duties and additional customs duties
Sales tax and federal excise duty
explanation: The policy commits to eliminating regulatory duties and additional customs duties over about five years.

text: The Special Investment Facilitation Council, created to fast-track foreign investment in Pakistan, was established in which year?
explanation: The Special Investment Facilitation Council was set up in June 2023 to coordinate investment in priority sectors such as minerals, agriculture, IT and energy.

text: The National Fiscal Pact, under which provinces committed to take on additional spending responsibilities and raise agricultural income tax, was signed in which year?
explanation: The National Fiscal Pact was signed by the federal government and the provinces in September 2024 as part of the IMF programme commitments.

text: The Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, created under legislation passed in 2025, regulates which sector?
explanation: PVARA was established under the 2025 virtual assets law to license and supervise virtual asset service providers.

text: The KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange recorded a gain of approximately what percentage during fiscal year 2025-26?
explanation: The KSE-100 rose about 44 percent during FY2025-26, outperforming other domestic asset classes for a third straight year.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, Pakistan's total liquid foreign exchange reserves in mid-May 2026 stood at approximately how much?
explanation: The Survey reported total liquid reserves of about US$22.6 billion on 15 May 2026, of which about US$17.1 billion was held by the State Bank.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, average consumer price inflation during July-April of FY2024-25 fell to approximately what level?
explanation: Average CPI inflation fell to about 4.7 percent during July-April FY2024-25, down from about 26 percent in the same period a year earlier.

text: According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26, average consumer price inflation during July-April of FY2025-26 rose to approximately what level?
explanation: Average CPI inflation was about 6.19 percent during July-April FY2025-26, up from about 4.73 percent a year earlier.

text: The Extended Fund Facility arrangement approved for Pakistan in 2024 was denominated in which unit of account?
explanation: IMF arrangements are denominated in Special Drawing Rights; Pakistan's arrangement was SDR 5,320 million, about US$7 billion.

text: Pakistan's federal budget for fiscal year 2025-26 was presented in which month?
explanation: The FY2025-26 federal budget was presented in June 2025, ahead of the fiscal year beginning on 1 July.

text: Pakistan's fiscal year for budget purposes runs between which dates?
explanation: Pakistan's fiscal year runs from 1 July to 30 June, so FY2025-26 ended on 30 June 2026.

text: Which institution publishes the Pakistan Economic Survey each year on the eve of the federal budget?
explanation: The Pakistan Economic Survey is issued by the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance a day before the budget is presented.

text: Which body in Pakistan takes the decision on the policy interest rate?
options: Monetary Policy Committee of the State Bank of Pakistan
explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee of the State Bank of Pakistan sets the policy rate at its scheduled meetings.

text: Which organisation compiles Pakistan's monthly merchandise trade statistics used to report annual export and import totals?
options: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
explanation: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics publishes the monthly and annual merchandise trade data on which the FY2025-26 figures were based.

text: The April 2025 militant attack that triggered the India-Pakistan crisis of that year took place at which location in Indian-administered Kashmir?
explanation: The attack on tourists at Pahalgam on 22 April 2025 killed 26 people and set off the diplomatic and military escalation between India and Pakistan.

text: India's military operation launched against Pakistan on 7 May 2025 was code-named:
explanation: India named its 7 May 2025 missile and air strikes on Pakistan and Azad Kashmir 'Operation Sindoor'.

text: Pakistan's retaliatory military operation launched on 10 May 2025 against India was code-named:
explanation: Pakistan named its 10 May 2025 tri-services response 'Bunyan-um-Marsoos', a Quranic phrase meaning a firmly cemented structure.

text: On which date did India launch Operation Sindoor against targets in Pakistan?
explanation: Operation Sindoor began in the early hours of 7 May 2025, about two weeks after the Pahalgam attack.

text: The ceasefire that ended the May 2025 armed conflict between India and Pakistan took effect on:
explanation: A ceasefire was announced and took effect on the evening of 10 May 2025, four days after hostilities began.

text: The head of state who publicly announced the India-Pakistan ceasefire of 10 May 2025 before either government did was the president of:
explanation: US President Donald Trump announced the ceasefire publicly on social media on 10 May 2025, crediting American mediation.

text: In Pakistan's official terminology, the May 2025 armed conflict with India is referred to as:
explanation: Pakistan officially designates the May 2025 conflict 'Marka-e-Haq' (the battle for truth); Bunyan-um-Marsoos was the name of the military operation within it.

text: Which treaty did India announce it would hold 'in abeyance' after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack?
explanation: India's Cabinet Committee on Security announced on 23 April 2025 that the Indus Waters Treaty would be held in abeyance with immediate effect.

text: In its statement of 24 April 2025, Pakistan's National Security Committee said it reserved the right to hold which agreement in abeyance?
explanation: Pakistan's National Security Committee responded to India's measures by stating it had the right to hold the 1972 Simla Agreement, and other bilateral accords, in abeyance.

text: Pakistan's National Security Committee statement of 24 April 2025 declared that any attempt to stop or divert Pakistan's share of Indus waters would be treated as:
options: A breach of the UN Charter only
explanation: The Committee stated that any attempt to stop or divert water belonging to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty would be considered an act of war.

text: Which body issued the supplemental award of 27 June 2025 holding that the Indus Waters Treaty does not permit a party to unilaterally place it in abeyance?
options: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
The Court of Arbitration constituted under the Indus Waters Treaty
explanation: The Court of Arbitration constituted under the Treaty, with the Permanent Court of Arbitration as registry, ruled on 27 June 2025 that India's abeyance did not affect the Court's competence.

text: Which land crossing with Pakistan did India announce it was closing after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack?
explanation: India ordered the closure of the Attari Integrated Check Post on the Attari-Wagah route as part of its 23 April 2025 measures.

text: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, the three rivers allocated to Pakistan are:
explanation: The Treaty gives Pakistan the western rivers - Indus, Jhelum and Chenab - while India receives the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

text: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in which year, with which institution as broker?
explanation: The Treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 after negotiations brokered by the World Bank, which is also a signatory for limited purposes.

text: Which Pakistan Army chief was promoted to the rank of Field Marshal on 20 May 2025?
explanation: The federal cabinet approved the promotion of General Syed Asim Munir to Field Marshal on 20 May 2025, citing his leadership during the conflict with India.

text: Asim Munir's elevation in May 2025 made him which Field Marshal in Pakistan's history?
explanation: He became Pakistan's second Field Marshal; the first was Ayub Khan, who assumed the rank in 1959.

text: The Pakistan-Afghanistan ceasefire of October 2025 was agreed at negotiations held in which city?
explanation: After a week of the worst border fighting in years, Pakistani and Afghan delegations agreed to an immediate ceasefire at talks in Doha.

text: Which two countries mediated the Pakistan-Afghanistan ceasefire agreed in October 2025?
explanation: Qatar and Türkiye jointly mediated the Doha talks that produced the October 2025 ceasefire between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

text: On what date was the Pakistan-Afghanistan ceasefire announced in Doha in 2025?
explanation: The immediate ceasefire was announced on 19 October 2025, following clashes that began around 11 October.

text: The follow-up rounds of Pakistan-Afghanistan negotiations after the October 2025 Doha ceasefire were hosted in which city?
explanation: Follow-up talks intended to build mechanisms for a durable peace were held in Istanbul, and broke down in November 2025 without agreement.

text: The boundary between Pakistan and Afghanistan, which Kabul has never formally recognised, is known as the:
explanation: The Durand Line, demarcated in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan, remains the de facto Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

text: The Torkham border crossing links Pakistan's Khyber district with which Afghan province?
explanation: Torkham is the busiest Pakistan-Afghanistan crossing, connecting Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Nangarhar province.

text: The Chaman border crossing connects Balochistan with which Afghan province?
explanation: Chaman in Balochistan faces Spin Boldak in Kandahar province, making it the second-busiest crossing on the Durand Line.

text: Pakistan's programme for the deportation of undocumented foreign nationals, under which large numbers of Afghans have been repatriated since 2023, is called the:
explanation: The Illegal Foreigners Repatriation Plan, announced in late 2023, has been implemented in phases covering undocumented migrants and later Afghan Citizen Card holders.

text: Pakistan's retaliatory strikes inside Iranian territory in January 2024 were code-named:
explanation: Pakistan carried out Operation Marg Bar Sarmachar on 18 January 2024 against Baloch separatist hideouts inside Iran, two days after Iranian strikes on Pakistani soil.

text: The Iranian strikes on Pakistani territory in January 2024 targeted alleged bases of which group?
explanation: Iran said its 16 January 2024 strikes in Balochistan targeted the Sunni militant group Jaish al-Adl, which operates across the Iran-Pakistan border.

text: Which Iranian president made a state visit to Pakistan in August 2025?
explanation: President Masoud Pezeshkian visited Islamabad on 2-3 August 2025, holding talks with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on trade and border security.

text: During the Iranian president's August 2025 visit to Islamabad, the two sides set a bilateral trade target of:
explanation: Pakistan and Iran agreed to raise annual bilateral trade to US$10 billion from roughly US$3 billion at the time.

text: The Taftan border crossing, Pakistan's main land route to Iran, lies in which province?
explanation: Taftan is in Chagai district of Balochistan and faces Mirjaveh on the Iranian side.

text: The flagship deep-sea port of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is located at:
explanation: Gwadar port in Balochistan is CPEC's flagship maritime project, operated under a Chinese concession.

text: Pakistan hosted a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in October 2024 in which city?
explanation: Islamabad hosted the 23rd meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government on 15-16 October 2024.

text: Which Chinese leader represented China at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting hosted by Pakistan in October 2024?
explanation: Premier Li Qiang led the Chinese delegation, as the Council of Heads of Government is a prime-ministerial-level SCO body.

text: In 2025 Pakistan and China agreed to advance the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor into which stage?
options: The Belt and Road pilot stage
explanation: During Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's China visit in 2025 the two governments reaffirmed an upgraded CPEC Phase-2, focused on industry, agriculture, mining and IT.

text: The 2025 SCO Council of Heads of State summit attended by Pakistan's prime minister was held in which Chinese city?
explanation: The SCO Heads of State summit was held in Tianjin on 31 August-1 September 2025, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attended.

text: Pakistan became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in which year?
explanation: Pakistan and India were admitted as full SCO members at the Astana summit in June 2017, having earlier been observers.

text: The trade agreement announced between Pakistan and the United States in July 2025 was presented as centring on joint development of Pakistan's:
explanation: President Trump announced the deal by highlighting cooperation on developing Pakistan's oil reserves alongside tariff relief for Pakistani exports.

text: The reciprocal tariff rate applied to Pakistani exports under the United States order of July 2025 was:
explanation: Pakistan's rate was set at 19 percent, lower than the 25 percent applied to India and 20 percent to Bangladesh at the time.

text: In March 2025 Pakistan handed over to the United States a suspect accused of planning which attack?
options: The Abbey Gate bombing at Kabul airport
explanation: Pakistan captured and transferred Mohammad Sharifullah, an Islamic State-Khorasan operative accused of planning the August 2021 Abbey Gate bombing that killed 13 US service members.

text: In June 2025 the Government of Pakistan announced it would formally recommend which figure for the Nobel Peace Prize?
explanation: Pakistan announced in June 2025 that it would nominate US President Donald Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize, citing his role in the May 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire.

text: Which Pakistani military officer was hosted for a working lunch at the White House by President Trump in June 2025?
options: Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu
explanation: Field Marshal Asim Munir was received at the White House in June 2025, an unusual honour for a serving army chief without a head of government present.

text: In December 2025 the Export-Import Bank of the United States approved financing of about US$1.25 billion for which Pakistani project?
explanation: US EXIM approved roughly US$1.25 billion in financing for the Reko Diq mining project, part of a wider debt package involving the IFC and ADB.

text: The Reko Diq copper and gold project, central to Pakistan's minerals diplomacy, is located in which province?
explanation: Reko Diq lies in Chagai district of Balochistan and is operated by Barrick alongside federal and provincial government shareholdings.

text: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in September 2025 in which city?
explanation: The agreement was signed at Al-Yamamah Palace in Riyadh on 17 September 2025 during Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's visit.

text: Who signed the Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement of September 2025 on behalf of Saudi Arabia?
explanation: Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman signed for Saudi Arabia, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signing for Pakistan.

text: The central clause of the Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement of 2025 states that:
options: Neither state may host foreign military bases
Both states will jointly develop nuclear energy
Each will station a permanent brigade in the other
Any aggression against either country shall be considered aggression against both
explanation: The agreement provides that aggression against either country shall be regarded as aggression against both, echoing collective-defence language.

text: Which UAE head of state made his first official visit to Pakistan as president in December 2025?
options: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed
explanation: President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan made his first official visit to Pakistan as UAE head of state in December 2025.

text: Pakistan's prime minister attended the October 2025 Gaza peace summit held at which Egyptian city?
explanation: The summit co-chaired by President Trump and President Sisi was held at Sharm el-Sheikh on 13 October 2025, with Shehbaz Sharif among the attending leaders.

text: Pakistan began a two-year term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council covering which period?
explanation: Pakistan's term as a non-permanent member of the Security Council runs from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026.

text: In the General Assembly election of June 2024, Pakistan won its Security Council seat with how many votes?
explanation: Pakistan secured 182 votes in the UN General Assembly, comfortably above the required two-thirds majority.

text: The 2025-2026 term is Pakistan's how-manieth term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council?
explanation: It is Pakistan's eighth term on the Security Council, one of the highest totals among Asian states.

text: Pakistan held the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council during which month of 2025?
explanation: Pakistan assumed the Security Council presidency for July 2025, the first of its two presidencies during the 2025-2026 term.

text: Which Security Council resolution on strengthening mechanisms for the peaceful settlement of disputes was adopted unanimously under Pakistan's presidency in July 2025?
explanation: Resolution 2788, sponsored by Pakistan, was adopted unanimously on 22 July 2025 during its Council presidency.

text: Who chaired the high-level Security Council debate on multilateralism and peaceful settlement of disputes for Pakistan in July 2025?
options: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar
explanation: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar presided over the signature events of Pakistan's July 2025 Council presidency.

text: In June 2025 Pakistan was appointed chair of the Security Council sanctions committee established under which resolution?
explanation: Pakistan chairs the committee created by Resolution 1988 (2011), which oversees sanctions measures relating to the Taliban.

text: Alongside chairing the Taliban sanctions committee, Pakistan was appointed vice-chair of which Security Council body for 2025?
options: The Committee on Admission of New Members
explanation: Pakistan was made a vice-chair of the Counter-Terrorism Committee, which monitors implementation of Resolution 1373 (2001).

text: Who succeeded Munir Akram as Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in 2025?
explanation: Asim Iftikhar Ahmad presented his credentials as Pakistan's Permanent Representative in April 2025 and led the mission during the July 2025 Council presidency.

text: The 17th ECO Summit, attended by Pakistan's prime minister in July 2025, was held in which city?
explanation: Azerbaijan hosted the 17th Economic Cooperation Organization summit at Khankendi on 3-4 July 2025.

text: The permanent secretariat of the Economic Cooperation Organization, of which Pakistan is a founding member, is located in:
explanation: The ECO secretariat is in Tehran; the organisation was founded in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as successor to the RCD.

text: The 51st session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers, attended by Pakistan in June 2025, was hosted by which city?
explanation: Türkiye hosted the 51st OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Istanbul on 21-22 June 2025 under the theme 'The OIC in a Transforming World'.

text: The General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is headquartered in:
explanation: The OIC General Secretariat has been based in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, pending the liberation of Jerusalem.

text: The most recent SAARC summit actually held was the 18th, convened in which capital?
explanation: The 18th SAARC summit was held in Kathmandu in November 2014; no summit has been held since.

text: The 19th SAARC summit, indefinitely postponed after several members withdrew, was scheduled to be hosted by which city?
explanation: Islamabad was to host the 19th SAARC summit in November 2016, but it was postponed after India and other members pulled out.

text: The 11th D-8 Summit, attended by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in December 2024, was held in which city?
explanation: Egypt hosted the 11th summit of the D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation in Cairo in December 2024 and assumed its chairmanship.

text: Azerbaijan signed an investment agreement with Pakistan on the sidelines of the July 2025 ECO Summit worth approximately:
explanation: Azerbaijan committed about US$2 billion of investment in Pakistan under an agreement signed during the Khankendi ECO Summit.

text: Which European head of state paid an official visit to Pakistan in November 2024, the first by a leader of his country in decades?
options: Milos Zeman of the Czech Republic
explanation: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko visited Pakistan on 25-27 November 2024, and several bilateral agreements were signed.

text: In July 2025 Pakistan and Russia signed an agreement in Moscow to revive which industrial facility?
explanation: The agreement, signed at Pakistan's embassy in Moscow, provides for Russian participation in restarting and expanding Pakistan Steel Mills in Karachi.

text: Ishaq Dar's visit to Dhaka in August 2025 was the first by a Pakistani foreign minister since which year?
explanation: It was described as the first visit by a Pakistani foreign minister to Bangladesh since 2012, and marked a thaw in bilateral ties.

text: In 2025 Pakistan established diplomatic relations, for the first time, with which country through an exchange of a joint communique at Tianjin?
explanation: Pakistan and Armenia exchanged a joint communique establishing diplomatic relations in 2025, ending Islamabad's long-standing non-recognition of Armenia.

text: Who was appointed Foreign Secretary of Pakistan in September 2024, becoming only the second woman to hold the office?
explanation: Amna Baloch took charge as Foreign Secretary in September 2024, following Tehmina Janjua as the second woman in the post.

text: On what date was the general election for Pakistan's National Assembly held in 2024?
explanation: The Election Commission of Pakistan held the general election for the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies on 8 February 2024.

text: How many directly elected general seats of Pakistan's National Assembly were contested in the 2024 general election?
explanation: The National Assembly has 266 general seats filled by direct election; the remaining 70 are reserved for women and non-Muslims.

text: How many National Assembly general seats did the Pakistan Muslim League (N) win in the 2024 general election?
explanation: PML-N took 75 general seats, the largest tally won under a party symbol, while PTI-backed candidates contested as independents.

text: How many National Assembly general seats did the Pakistan Peoples Party win in the 2024 general election?
explanation: The PPP won 54 general seats and joined the PML-N-led coalition government formed after the election.

text: Which electoral symbol was Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf denied for the 2024 general election after a Supreme Court ruling in January 2024?
explanation: On 13 January 2024 the Supreme Court set aside the Peshawar High Court order and restored the ECP decision withdrawing the bat symbol over defective intra-party elections.

text: After the 2024 general election, most PTI-backed independent members of the National Assembly joined which party?
explanation: Having contested as independents, PTI-backed winners joined the Sunni Ittehad Council in order to claim reserved seats.

text: How many votes did Shehbaz Sharif secure when the National Assembly elected him Prime Minister on 3 March 2024?
explanation: Shehbaz Sharif polled 201 votes against 92 for his rival, comfortably above the 169 needed for a majority.

text: Who was the rival candidate defeated by Shehbaz Sharif in the March 2024 election for Prime Minister?
explanation: Omar Ayub Khan was the joint candidate of the PTI-backed Sunni Ittehad Council and received 92 votes.

text: Who won Pakistan's presidential election held on 9 March 2024?
explanation: Asif Ali Zardari of the PPP secured 411 electoral votes to win a second, non-consecutive term as President.

text: Who was the opposition-backed candidate in Pakistan's 2024 presidential election?
explanation: The PTI-backed Sunni Ittehad Council nominated PkMAP chief Mahmood Khan Achakzai, who lost to Asif Ali Zardari.

text: Asif Ali Zardari, elected in March 2024, is which numbered President of Pakistan?
explanation: Zardari became the 14th President of Pakistan and the first civilian to be elected to the office twice.

text: Who was appointed Deputy Prime Minister of Pakistan in April 2024?
explanation: Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar was given the additional charge of Deputy Prime Minister in late April 2024.

text: Who presented Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27 in the National Assembly?
explanation: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb presented the 2026-27 federal budget on 12 June 2026.

text: Who was elected Speaker of Pakistan's National Assembly in March 2024?
explanation: PML-N's Sardar Ayaz Sadiq was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024, returning to an office he had held before.

text: Who was elected Deputy Speaker of Pakistan's National Assembly in March 2024?
explanation: The PPP's Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah was elected Deputy Speaker alongside Speaker Ayaz Sadiq on 1 March 2024.

text: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, elected in 2024, became which numbered Speaker of Pakistan's National Assembly?
explanation: He was sworn in as the 23rd Speaker of the National Assembly following the 2024 general election.

text: Who was elected Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan in April 2024?
explanation: Former Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gillani of the PPP was elected Chairman of the Senate on 9 April 2024.

text: Who was elected Deputy Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan in April 2024?
explanation: Syedaal Khan Nasar was elected Deputy Chairman in the same sitting that elected Yousaf Raza Gillani as Chairman.

text: Who was notified as Leader of the Opposition in Pakistan's National Assembly in January 2026?
explanation: Achakzai was appointed in January 2026, filling a vacancy left after Omar Ayub Khan lost his seat on conviction in 2025.

text: Mahmood Khan Achakzai heads which political party?
explanation: Achakzai is chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP), based mainly in Pashtun districts of Balochistan.

text: Which opposition alliance launched in 2024 is led by Mahmood Khan Achakzai?
explanation: Tehreek Tahafuz Ayin-e-Pakistan, a PTI-backed alliance for the defence of the Constitution, was launched from Pishin in 2024 under Achakzai.

text: Who was appointed Leader of the Opposition in Pakistan's National Assembly in 2024 after the general election?
explanation: PTI's Omar Ayub Khan was notified as Opposition Leader in the National Assembly in March 2024.

text: Who was appointed Leader of the Opposition in the Senate of Pakistan in April 2024?
explanation: PTI senator Shibli Faraz took over as Senate Opposition Leader after the March-April 2024 Senate elections.

text: In which month and year was the 26th Constitutional Amendment passed by Pakistan's Parliament?
explanation: The Senate passed it on 20 October 2024 and the National Assembly on 21 October 2024; the President assented the same day.

text: The 26th Constitutional Amendment provided for the creation of which body inside the Supreme Court of Pakistan?
explanation: The amendment set up a separate Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court to hear constitutional matters.

text: Which body was empowered by the 26th Amendment to nominate the Chief Justice of Pakistan from among the three most senior Supreme Court judges?
explanation: The amendment ended automatic elevation by seniority and gave the nomination to a 12-member Special Parliamentary Committee voting by two-thirds majority.

text: What tenure did the 26th Amendment fix for the Chief Justice of Pakistan?
explanation: Article 177 was amended to cap the Chief Justice's term at three years, subject to the retirement age.

text: Which fundamental right was inserted into Pakistan's Constitution as Article 9A by the 26th Amendment?
options: Right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment
explanation: Article 9A makes a clean, healthy and sustainable environment a justiciable fundamental right.

text: By which date does the 26th Amendment require riba (usury) to be eliminated in Pakistan, as far as practicable?
explanation: The amendment wrote into the Constitution a deadline of 1 January 2028 for the elimination of riba as far as practicable.

text: Who took oath in October 2024 as the first Chief Justice of Pakistan appointed under the 26th Amendment?
explanation: Justice Yahya Afridi was nominated by the Special Parliamentary Committee and sworn in on 26 October 2024.

text: Justice Yahya Afridi became which numbered Chief Justice of Pakistan?
explanation: He is counted as the 30th Chief Justice of Pakistan, succeeding Qazi Faez Isa.

text: On what date did President Asif Ali Zardari give assent to Pakistan's 27th Constitutional Amendment?
explanation: The Senate approved the final text on 13 November 2025 and the President signed it into law the same day.

text: By what margin did the Senate finally pass Pakistan's 27th Constitutional Amendment in November 2025?
explanation: The Senate recorded 64 votes in favour and 4 against, exactly meeting the two-thirds threshold of 64 in a house of 96.

text: How many votes were cast in favour of the 27th Constitutional Amendment in Pakistan's National Assembly?
explanation: The National Assembly passed the bill on 12 November 2025 with 234 votes in favour against 4, comfortably above the 224 required.

text: Which federal minister tabled the 27th Constitutional Amendment bill in Pakistan's Parliament?
explanation: Law and Justice Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar moved the bill on behalf of the government.

text: Which new court was established by Pakistan's 27th Constitutional Amendment?
explanation: The amendment created a Federal Constitutional Court and moved constitutional jurisdiction to it from the Supreme Court.

text: Who was appointed the first Chief Justice of Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court in November 2025?
explanation: Justice Aminuddin Khan, who had headed the Supreme Court's Constitutional Bench, was named the first Chief Justice of the new court.

text: What is the sanctioned strength of judges of Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court?
explanation: The court was given a sanctioned strength of 13 judges including its Chief Justice.

text: Which article of Pakistan's Constitution was amended by the 27th Amendment to create the office of Chief of Defence Forces?
explanation: Article 243, which deals with command of the armed forces, was recast to provide for a Chief of Defence Forces.

text: Which military office was abolished by Pakistan's 27th Constitutional Amendment?
options: Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
explanation: The post of Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee lapsed on 27 November 2025 and its role passed to the new Chief of Defence Forces.

text: Who was the last holder of the office of Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee of Pakistan?
explanation: General Sahir Shamshad Mirza retired on 27 November 2025, after which the office ceased to exist.

text: Who became Pakistan's first Chief of Defence Forces?
options: Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Babar
explanation: Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of Army Staff, was appointed to the newly created post of Chief of Defence Forces in late 2025.

text: What change did Pakistan's 27th Amendment make to Article 248 in relation to the President?
options: It limited immunity to five years after leaving office
It made immunity conditional on parliamentary approval
It granted lifetime immunity from criminal and civil proceedings
explanation: Immunity under Article 248, previously tied to the term of office, was extended to cover the President for life.

text: Which two Supreme Court judges resigned on 13 November 2025 in protest against the 27th Constitutional Amendment?
options: Mansoor Ali Shah and Athar Minallah
Aminuddin Khan and Naeem Akhtar Afghan
Yahya Afridi and Irfan Saadat Khan
explanation: Justices Mansoor Ali Shah and Athar Minallah resigned the day the amendment received presidential assent.

text: How many judges sat on the Supreme Court bench that delivered the reserved seats verdict of 12 July 2024?
explanation: A 13-member full court decided the reserved seats case, with eight judges forming the majority in favour of PTI.

text: Which judge headed the Supreme Court constitutional bench that decided the reserved seats review in 2025?
explanation: Justice Aminuddin Khan presided over the constitutional bench that took up review petitions against the July 2024 judgment.

text: What did the Supreme Court's constitutional bench decide in the reserved seats review of March 2025?
options: That PTI was not entitled to the reserved seats
That PTI was entitled to all the reserved seats
That the reserved seats would remain vacant
That fresh elections would be held for the reserved seats
explanation: The bench accepted the review petitions on 26 March 2025 and held that PTI could not claim reserved seats because it had not contested the election as a party.

text: Which provision of the Pakistan Army Act 1952 permitting trial of civilians was restored by the Supreme Court's constitutional bench in May 2025?
explanation: The constitutional bench overturned the October 2023 judgment and revived Section 2(1)(d), under which civilians may be tried by court martial.

text: In September 2024 the Supreme Court reversed its earlier judgment and reinstated amendments to which law?
explanation: The Court restored the 2022 amendments to the accountability law, including the Rs 500 million threshold for NAB's jurisdiction.

text: Who was sworn in as Chief Justice of the Islamabad High Court in July 2025?
explanation: Justice Sarfraz Dogar, transferred from the Lahore High Court, took oath as Chief Justice of the Islamabad High Court amid a seniority dispute.

text: In which case was Imran Khan sentenced to 14 years' imprisonment in January 2025?
explanation: An accountability court in Rawalpindi convicted him on 17 January 2025 in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust reference.

text: In December 2025 Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi were each sentenced to how many years in the Toshakhana-II case?
explanation: A special court handed both a 17-year sentence on 20 December 2025 in the second Toshakhana reference.

text: Who became the first woman Chief Minister of Punjab in February 2024?
explanation: Maryam Nawaz Sharif was elected on 26 February 2024, becoming the first woman to head any Pakistani province.

text: How many votes did Maryam Nawaz secure in the Punjab Assembly to be elected Chief Minister in February 2024?
explanation: She polled 220 votes in the Punjab Assembly while the opposition boycotted the count.

text: Who was elected Chief Minister of Sindh for a third consecutive term in February 2024?
explanation: PPP's Syed Murad Ali Shah was elected Sindh Chief Minister for a third successive term on 26 February 2024.

text: Who was elected Chief Minister of Balochistan in early 2024?
explanation: PPP's Mir Sarfraz Bugti was elected unopposed as Chief Minister of Balochistan after the 2024 general election.

text: Who became Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa after Pakistan's 2024 general election?
explanation: PTI's Ali Amin Gandapur was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in March 2024.

text: Who was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025?
explanation: PTI replaced Ali Amin Gandapur with Sohail Afridi, who was elected by the provincial assembly on 13 October 2025.

text: Which court in October 2025 ordered the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to administer the oath of office to Sohail Afridi?
explanation: The Peshawar High Court directed Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to administer the oath by 15 October 2025 after his delay.

text: Who took oath as Governor of Punjab in May 2024?
explanation: PPP's Sardar Saleem Haider Khan was sworn in as the 40th Governor of Punjab in May 2024.

text: Who took oath as Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in May 2024?
explanation: PPP leader Faisal Karim Kundi was sworn in as Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in May 2024.

text: Who took oath as Governor of Balochistan in May 2024?
explanation: Sheikh Jaffar Khan Mandokhail was sworn in as Governor of Balochistan in May 2024.

text: Who was elected Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab in 2024?
explanation: PML-N's Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan was elected Speaker of the Punjab Assembly after the 2024 election.

text: Who was elected Speaker of the Sindh Assembly in 2024?
explanation: PPP's Syed Awais Qadir Shah was elected Speaker of the Sindh Assembly following the 2024 general election.

text: Who was sworn in as Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir in November 2025?
explanation: Faisal Mumtaz Rathore was elected the 16th Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir and took oath on 18 November 2025.

text: Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who became Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir in 2025, belongs to which party?
options: All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference
explanation: Rathore is a PPP leader and replaced Chaudhry Anwarul Haq as head of the AJK government.

text: On what date was the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly election held in 2026?
explanation: Polling for the Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly took place on 7 June 2026 after a caretaker set-up ran the region.

text: Which party won the largest number of general seats in the 2026 Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly election?
explanation: The PPP won 10 general seats, ahead of PML-N's six, and later formed a coalition government with PML-N.

text: Who was elected Chief Minister of Gilgit-Baltistan in June 2026?
explanation: PPP's Amjad Hussain Azar was elected unopposed on 22 June 2026 under a power-sharing deal with PML-N.

text: Who was appointed caretaker Chief Minister of Gilgit-Baltistan in November 2025?
explanation: Justice (retd) Yar Muhammad was sworn in as caretaker Chief Minister on 25 November 2025 to oversee the 2026 election.

text: The Senate election of 2 April 2024 left the seats of which province unfilled because its assembly was incomplete?
explanation: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Senate seats could not be filled in April 2024 because the reserved seats dispute had left the provincial assembly short of members.

text: In which month of 2025 were the long-delayed Senate elections for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa finally held?
explanation: Polling for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Senate seats took place on 21 July 2025 after the reserved seats issue was settled.

text: On what date were by-elections held in 2025 for six National Assembly and seven Punjab Assembly seats?
explanation: The by-elections of 23 November 2025 filled seats vacated mainly by the disqualification of PTI members convicted over the May 2023 riots.

text: Which party won the overwhelming majority of seats in Pakistan's by-elections of 23 November 2025?
explanation: PML-N took 12 of the 13 seats contested, with PTI winning only one.

text: Which section inserted by Pakistan's PECA (Amendment) Act 2025 criminalises the spreading of false or fake information?
explanation: Section 26A of the amended Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act penalises intentionally spreading information known to be false or fake.

text: Which of these bodies was created by Pakistan's PECA (Amendment) Act 2025?
explanation: The 2025 amendment set up a Social Media Protection Tribunal along with a regulatory authority and a complaint council.

text: In which month and year did President Zardari give assent to Pakistan's PECA (Amendment) Act?
explanation: The President signed the PECA amendment into law at the end of January 2025 despite protests by journalists' bodies.

text: Which authority was established by Pakistan's Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025?
explanation: The Digital Nation Pakistan Act, enacted in January 2025, created the Pakistan Digital Authority to drive digital transformation.

text: Who chairs the National Digital Commission created under Pakistan's Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025?
options: The Governor of the State Bank
explanation: The Act places the National Digital Commission, which sets strategic direction for the Pakistan Digital Authority, under the Prime Minister's chairmanship.

text: What is the name of the five-year National Economic Transformation Plan launched by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on 31 December 2024?
explanation: Uraan Pakistan is the National Economic Transformation Plan 2024-29 launched on 31 December 2024.

text: What are the five pillars of Pakistan's Uraan Pakistan plan collectively called?
explanation: The plan is built on the 5Es: Exports, E-Pakistan, Environment and climate, Energy and infrastructure, and Equity and empowerment.

text: What annual export target does Pakistan's Uraan Pakistan plan set for 2029?
explanation: Uraan Pakistan aims to roughly double annual exports to about US$60 billion by 2029.

text: What was the total outlay of Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27?
explanation: The 2026-27 federal budget presented on 12 June 2026 carried a total outlay of roughly Rs 18,771 billion.

text: What GDP growth rate did Pakistan's federal budget for 2026-27 target?
explanation: The 2026-27 budget set a real GDP growth target of 4 per cent.

text: What was the total outlay of Pakistan's federal budget for 2025-26, presented on 10 June 2025?
explanation: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb presented a budget of about Rs 17,573 billion for 2025-26.

text: What is the name of the reinvigorated counter-terrorism campaign approved by Pakistan's government in June 2024?
explanation: Operation Azm-e-Istehkam was approved on 22 June 2024 as a reinvigorated national counter-terrorism drive.

text: Which forum approved Operation Azm-e-Istehkam in June 2024?
options: The Central Apex Committee of the National Action Plan
explanation: The Central Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, approved the campaign.

text: Under the National Fiscal Pact agreed by Pakistan's federal and provincial governments in September 2024, the provinces undertook to tax which income?
explanation: The pact, signed under the IMF programme, committed provinces to align agricultural income tax with federal personal and corporate rates.

text: At which Islamabad location did the PTI protest of November 2024 culminate before being dispersed?
explanation: PTI marchers reached D-Chowk near the Red Zone on 26 November 2024 before a night-time crackdown ended the protest.

text: Which official was named in January 2020 as Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan for a five-year term?
explanation: Sikandar Sultan Raja was appointed Chief Election Commissioner on 27 January 2020 and oversaw the 2024 general election.
